import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.45

by D. M. Smirnov

Does the $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups coincide with the
$Q$-theory of a single finitely presented group?

Here a quasi-identity is a universal Horn sentence in the language of groups,
with finitely many variables and finitely many premises. The $Q$-theory of a
class is the set of quasi-identities true in every member of the class.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.45»

/-- A quasi-identity in the language of groups, with `numVariables` variables.
Each pair in `premises` is an equation between group words, and `conclusion`
is the consequent equation. The empty list of premises gives an identity. -/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  numVariables : ℕ
  premises : List (FreeGroup (Fin numVariables) × FreeGroup (Fin numVariables))
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin numVariables) × FreeGroup (Fin numVariables)

/-- A group satisfies a quasi-identity if every assignment of its variables
that satisfies all premise equations also satisfies the conclusion equation. -/
def QuasiIdentity.IsSatisfiedBy (q : QuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ f : Fin q.numVariables → G,
    (∀ e ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift f e.1 = FreeGroup.lift f e.2) →
      FreeGroup.lift f q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift f q.conclusion.2

/--
Does the $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups coincide with the
$Q$-theory of a single finitely presented group?

The witness is presented using `n` generators and the finite set `rels` of
relations. The right-hand side is the intersection of the $Q$-theories of all
finite groups.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.45» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
      ∀ q : QuasiIdentity,
        q.IsSatisfiedBy (PresentedGroup (↑rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) ↔
          ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], q.IsSatisfiedBy G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.45»
modeling_decisions: A quasi-identity with n variables is represented by finitely many premise equations and one conclusion equation between elements of the free group on Fin n; satisfaction evaluates these words with FreeGroup.lift under every variable assignment.
The Q-theory of all finite groups is expressed semantically by quantifying over every type G equipped with Group G and Finite G, avoiding any need to package theories as sets.

A finitely presented witness is represented directly as PresentedGroup of a Finset of relators in the free group on Fin n. This enforces finitely many generators and relations and is equivalent, up to group isomorphism, to existentially quantifying an abstract finitely presented group.

$Q$-theory of a single finitely presented group?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

namespace Kourovka.«7.45»

/-- A group $G$ satisfies the displayed quasi-identity if every assignment of
its $n$ variables that satisfies all $m$ premise equations also satisfies the
conclusion equation. The words are elements of the free group on `Fin n`. -/
def SatisfiesQuasiIdentity {G : Type*} [Group G] {n m : ℕ}
    (premises : Fin m → FreeGroup (Fin n) × FreeGroup (Fin n))
    (conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin n) × FreeGroup (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ assignment : Fin n → G,
    (∀ i, FreeGroup.lift assignment (premises i).1 =
      FreeGroup.lift assignment (premises i).2) →
    FreeGroup.lift assignment conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift assignment conclusion.2

/-- A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a finite-rank free
group modulo the normal closure of finitely many relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresentedGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n m : ℕ, ∃ relators : Fin m → FreeGroup (Fin n),
    Nonempty (G ≃* FreeGroup (Fin n) ⧸ Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range relators))

/--
Does there exist a single finitely presented group whose $Q$-theory is exactly
the $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups? Here a quasi-identity is a
universal Horn sentence with finitely many variables and finitely many premise
equations; zero premises are allowed, so identities are included. A
quasi-identity belongs to the $Q$-theory of all finite groups precisely when it
holds in every finite group.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.45» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), IsFinitelyPresentedGroup G ∧
      ∀ (n m : ℕ)
        (premises : Fin m → FreeGroup (Fin n) × FreeGroup (Fin n))
        (conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin n) × FreeGroup (Fin n)),
        SatisfiesQuasiIdentity (G := G) premises conclusion ↔
          ∀ (H : Type) (_ : Group H) (_ : Finite H),
            SatisfiesQuasiIdentity (G := H) premises conclusion := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.45»
modeling_decisions: A quasi-identity with n variables and m premises is represented by pairs of words in the free group on Fin n, with premises indexed by Fin m and one conclusion equation.
Satisfaction universally quantifies assignments of the variables into the group and evaluates words with FreeGroup.lift.
Both n and m range over all natural numbers; in particular, m = 0 includes identities as required.
The Q-theory of all finite groups is represented pointwise by universal quantification over group types carrying a Finite instance.
A finitely presented group is represented as a group isomorphic to a quotient of FreeGroup (Fin n) by the normal closure of the range of a Fin m-indexed relator family.

/-!
# Conjecture 7.45

by D. M. Smirnov

Does the $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups (in the sense of 2.40) coincide with
the $Q$-theory of a single finitely presented group?

Following Mal'cev (Problem 2.40 of the notebook), a *quasi-identity* in the language of
groups is a universal Horn sentence
$$\forall x_1 \dots x_n \;
  \bigl(u_1(\bar x) = v_1(\bar x) \wedge \dots \wedge u_m(\bar x) = v_m(\bar x)
  \;\to\; u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)\bigr),$$
where $m \ge 0$ and $u_1, v_1, \dots, u_m, v_m, u, v$ are group words in the finitely many
variables $x_1, \dots, x_n$ (identities are the quasi-identities with $m = 0$).
The $Q$-theory of a class $\mathfrak{K}$ of groups is the set of all quasi-identities that
are true in every group of $\mathfrak{K}$; the $Q$-theory of a single group $G$ is the
$Q$-theory of the class $\{G\}$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.45»

/--
A quasi-identity in the language of groups, in the variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$:
$$\forall \bar x \;
  \bigl(u_1(\bar x) = v_1(\bar x) \wedge \dots \wedge u_m(\bar x) = v_m(\bar x)
  \;\to\; u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)\bigr).$$
The group words $u_i, v_i, u, v$ are recorded as elements of the free group on `Fin n`;
two group words define the same element of the free group exactly when they take the same
value in every group, so this loses nothing. The list of premises may be empty, in which
case the quasi-identity is an identity.
-/
structure GroupQuasiIdentity where
  /-- The number $n$ of variables. -/
  numVars : ℕ
  /-- The premises $u_1 = v_1, \dots, u_m = v_m$, as pairs of group words. -/
  premises : List (FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars))
  /-- The conclusion $u = v$, as a pair of group words. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars)

/--
A quasi-identity $\forall \bar x\,(\bigwedge_i u_i(\bar x) = v_i(\bar x) \to u(\bar x) = v(\bar x))$
holds in a group $G$ if for every assignment $\bar x$ of values in $G$ to the variables,
$u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)$ whenever $u_i(\bar x) = v_i(\bar x)$ for all $i$.
-/
def GroupQuasiIdentity.Holds (q : GroupQuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin q.numVars → G,
    (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x p.1 = FreeGroup.lift x p.2) →
      FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.2

/-- The $Q$-theory of a group $G$: the set of all quasi-identities that hold in $G$. -/
def qTheory (G : Type*) [Group G] : Set GroupQuasiIdentity :=
  {q | q.Holds G}

/--
The $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups: the set of all quasi-identities that hold
in every finite group, i.e. the intersection of the $Q$-theories of all finite groups.
-/
def qTheoryFiniteGroups : Set GroupQuasiIdentity :=
  {q | ∀ (H : Type) [Group H] [Finite H], q.Holds H}

/--
A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many
generators and finitely many defining relations.
-/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/--
Does the $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups (in the sense of 2.40) coincide with
the $Q$-theory of a single finitely presented group?

That is: is there a finitely presented group $G$ such that a quasi-identity holds in $G$ if
and only if it holds in every finite group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.45» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ qTheory G = qTheoryFiniteGroups := by
  sorry

/-- Every quasi-identity holds in the trivial group. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem GroupQuasiIdentity.holds_unit (q : GroupQuasiIdentity) : q.Holds Unit :=
  fun _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- The $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups is contained in the $Q$-theory of each
finite group. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem qTheoryFiniteGroups_subset_qTheory (H : Type) [Group H] [Finite H] :
    qTheoryFiniteGroups ⊆ qTheory H :=
  fun _ hq => hq H

/-- A group given by finitely many generators and relations is finitely presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))
    (h : rels.Finite) : IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup rels) :=
  ⟨n, rels, h, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- The quasi-identity $\forall x\,(x^2 = 1 \to x = 1)$. -/
def squareQuasiIdentity : GroupQuasiIdentity where
  numVars := 1
  premises := [(FreeGroup.of 0 ^ 2, 1)]
  conclusion := (FreeGroup.of 0, 1)

/-- The quasi-identity $\forall x\,(x^2 = 1 \to x = 1)$ fails in the group of order two, so it
does not belong to the $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem squareQuasiIdentity_not_mem_qTheoryFiniteGroups :
    squareQuasiIdentity ∉ qTheoryFiniteGroups := by
  intro h
  have := h (Multiplicative (ZMod 2)) (fun _ => Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)
  simp [squareQuasiIdentity] at this
  exact this (by decide)

/-- The quasi-identity $\forall x\,(x^2 = 1 \to x = 1)$ holds in the infinite cyclic group. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem squareQuasiIdentity_holds_int : squareQuasiIdentity.Holds (Multiplicative ℤ) := by
  intro x hx
  simpa [squareQuasiIdentity] using hx

end Kourovka.«7.45»

$$\forall x_1 \dots x_k \; \bigl(u_1(\bar x) = v_1(\bar x) \wedge \dots \wedge
u_n(\bar x) = v_n(\bar x) \;\to\; u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)\bigr),$$

(so identities are quasi-identities). The *$Q$-theory* of a class $\mathfrak{K}$ of groups
is the set of all quasi-identities that hold in every group of $\mathfrak{K}$; the $Q$-theory
of a single group $G$ is the $Q$-theory of $\{G\}$.

and a finitely presented group as `PresentedGroup rels` for a finite set `rels` of relators
in `FreeGroup (Fin k)`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

A quasi-identity in the language of groups: a universal Horn sentence
$$\forall x_1 \dots x_k \; \bigl(u_1(\bar x) = v_1(\bar x) \wedge \dots \wedge
u_n(\bar x) = v_n(\bar x) \;\to\; u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)\bigr)$$
with finitely many variables $x_1, \dots, x_k$ and finitely many premises ($n \geq 0$).
The words $u_i, v_i, u, v$ are elements of the free group on the $k$ variables.
-/

  numVars : ℕ
  /-- The number $n$ of premises. -/
  numPremises : ℕ

  premises : Fin numPremises → FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars)

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.45

by D. M. Smirnov

Does the $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups (in the sense of 2.40) coincide with the
$Q$-theory of a single finitely presented group?

Following Mal'cev (Kourovka 2.40), a *quasi-identity* in the language of groups is a universal
Horn sentence
$$\forall x_1 \dots x_n \;
  \bigl(u_1(\bar x) = v_1(\bar x) \wedge \dots \wedge u_m(\bar x) = v_m(\bar x)\bigr)
  \to u(\bar x) = v(\bar x),$$
where $m \geq 0$ and $u_i, v_i, u, v$ are group words in the variables $x_1, \dots, x_n$
(so identities, the case $m = 0$, are quasi-identities). The *$Q$-theory* of a class of groups
is the set of all quasi-identities true in every group of the class.

Group words are represented as elements of the free group `FreeGroup (Fin n)`. Two words that
are equal in the free group take the same value under every assignment in every group, so this
identification does not change which quasi-identities hold in a given group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.45»

/--
A quasi-identity in the language of groups: a universal Horn sentence
$\forall x_1 \dots x_n \; (\bigwedge_i u_i(\bar x) = v_i(\bar x)) \to u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)$
with finitely many variables and finitely many (possibly zero) premises. The words
$u_i, v_i, u, v$ are elements of the free group on the variables `Fin n`.
-/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The number `n` of variables $x_1, \dots, x_n$. -/
  numVars : ℕ
  /-- The finite list of premises $u_i(\bar x) = v_i(\bar x)$, as pairs of words. -/
  premises : List (FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars))
  /-- The conclusion $u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)$, as a pair of words. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars)

/--
A quasi-identity `q` holds in a group `G` if for every assignment `x` of the variables in `G`,
whenever all premises of `q` are satisfied, so is its conclusion. Words are evaluated at `x`
via `FreeGroup.lift x`.
-/
def QuasiIdentity.Holds (q : QuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin q.numVars → G,
    (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x p.1 = FreeGroup.lift x p.2) →
      FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.2

/-- The $Q$-theory of a group `G`: the set of all quasi-identities true in `G`. -/
def qTheory (G : Type*) [Group G] : Set QuasiIdentity :=
  {q | q.Holds G}

/--
The $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups: the set of all quasi-identities true in every
finite group.
-/
def qTheoryOfFiniteGroups : Set QuasiIdentity :=
  {q | ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], q.Holds G}

/--
A group `G` is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to the group `PresentedGroup rels`
given by finitely many generators `Fin n` and a finite set `rels` of relations.
-/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) ≃* G)

/-- Every quasi-identity holds in a trivial group. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 20]
lemma QuasiIdentity.holds_of_subsingleton (q : QuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G]
    [Subsingleton G] : q.Holds G :=
  fun _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- The $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups is contained in the $Q$-theory of any
finite group. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 20]
lemma qTheoryOfFiniteGroups_subset_qTheory (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    qTheoryOfFiniteGroups ⊆ qTheory G :=
  fun _ hq => hq G

/-- A finitely presented group is finitely generated. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsFinitelyPresented G) : Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  have : Group.FG (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
    Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨Set.range (PresentedGroup.of (rels := (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))),
      PresentedGroup.closure_range_of _, Set.finite_range _⟩
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.toMonoidHom) e.surjective

/--
Does the $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups (in the sense of 2.40) coincide with the
$Q$-theory of a single finitely presented group?

That is, does there exist a finitely presented group $G$ whose set of true quasi-identities is
exactly the set of quasi-identities true in every finite group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.45» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ qTheory G = qTheoryOfFiniteGroups := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.45»
